NAME: Industry Clean Operating Profit
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(oibdp, at))), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), DELTA(lct, 1)), SUB(ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1)), dp)), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating profitability should be more persistent and return-predictive when it is high relative to industry peers and not supported by balance-sheet accrual expansion.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This uses a continuous accrual-quality leg rather than a binary cash-flow gate, so profitable high-accrual firms can form an economically interpretable short side. The balance-sheet accrual construction avoids relying only on ib and oancf, while industry adjustment reduces the chance that the signal is just sector profitability or sector working-capital structure.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Persistent Profit Accrual Deterioration
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(ADD(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), DELTA(lct, 1)), SUB(ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1)), dp)), at), 3), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistently profitable firms should underperform when their accrual intensity is trending upward.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: A rising balance-sheet accrual trend indicates that an otherwise strong operating-profit record is becoming increasingly dependent on accounting working-capital expansion. Using a trend rather than second differences reduces measurement noise while still targeting deterioration in earnings quality.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Gross Profit Working Capital Absorption
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(NEG(ADD(recch, invch)), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High gross profitability should be less durable when it coincides with receivable and inventory cash absorption.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Compustat recch and invch are cash-flow-statement impacts, so negative values indicate receivable or inventory buildup; applying NEG correctly treats that buildup as a bad accrual-quality signal. The profitability leg focuses on gross economics, while the accrual leg asks whether those gross profits are being converted into cash rather than tied up in customers and inventory.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Pretax Profit Tax Payable Confirmation
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Pretax profitability is more credible when it is not accompanied by rising tax payables.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Firms reporting strong pretax income while accumulating unpaid tax liabilities may have a larger accounting timing component in earnings. This signal rewards profitable firms whose tax obligations appear to be settled rather than deferred through accrual buildup.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Intangible Adjusted Clean Profit
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), DELTA(lct, 1)), SUB(ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1)), dp)), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitability adjusted for expensed R&D should be most return-predictive when it is supported by low balance-sheet accruals.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Adding back R&D recognizes that some firms with durable economic profitability expense intangible investment immediately. The accrual-quality interaction separates genuinely productive intangible investors from firms whose apparent profitability depends on working-capital and other accrual expansion.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Stable Accrual EBITDA Confirmation
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(ebitda, at), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), DELTA(lct, 1)), SUB(ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1)), dp)), at), 1)), NEG(WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(ADD(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), DELTA(lct, 1)), SUB(ADD(DELTA(dlc, 1), DELTA(txp, 1)), dp)), at), 3), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistent EBITDA profitability should earn stronger abnormal returns when accruals are both low and stable.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The profitability leg smooths EBITDA to emphasize durable operating performance rather than a one-year spike. The accrual leg combines low accrual intensity with low accrual volatility, aiming to identify firms whose profits repeatedly convert into cash rather than depending on unstable accounting adjustments.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE Industry Clean Operating Profit---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially the product of two canonical published anomalies (operating profitability and Sloan balance-sheet accruals) with no novel conditioning mechanism, and the IND_RANK(IND_ADJ(...)) double industry normalization is redundant, making the profitability leg a near-monotone transform of itself.

---CRITIQUE Persistent Profit Accrual Deterioration---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The trend-in-accruals conditioning leg is a defensible earnings-quality deterioration measure and the sign convention is internally consistent (profitability enters only as a magnitude scaler), though it remains a close relative of the archive's accrual-gated profitability signal and the 3-period TREND on differenced balance-sheet items will be noisy.

---CRITIQUE Gross Profit Working Capital Absorption---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 1
RATIONALE: Up to a symmetric winsorization, IND_ZSCORE of the negated ratio equals minus the archive's leg, so with the expected sign also flipped this is the identical already-tested "Gross Profit Collection Quality" signal (fmb_tstat 0.65) relabeled rather than a new hypothesis.

---CRITIQUE Pretax Profit Tax Payable Confirmation---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The conditioning variable is economically thin and arguably signed backwards — rising taxes payable often reflects genuinely high current taxable income, which the tax-based earnings-quality literature treats as confirming rather than contaminating reported profits — and Δtxp is already a component of the working-capital accrual measures used elsewhere in this batch.

---CRITIQUE Intangible Adjusted Clean Profit---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is proposal 1 with R&D added back to the numerator, i.e., a cosmetic variant layering a second known adjustment (intangible-adjusted profitability) onto the same accruals interaction, and COALESCE(xrd,0) additionally conflates true zero R&D with non-reporters.

---CRITIQUE Stable Accrual EBITDA Confirmation---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Conditioning smoothed profitability on both the level and the volatility of accruals is the most substantively differentiated idea in the batch and internally coherent, but the 3-period VOL of twice-differenced balance-sheet items will be noisy and the stacked lag requirements risk pushing coverage below the archive's already thin ~10%.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Margin Expansion Asset Discipline
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(act, che), 1), sale), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating margin improvement is more durable when it is not accompanied by noncash current-asset buildup.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This replaces the generic operating-profitability × Sloan-accrual product with a more specific mechanism: margin expansion is credible only if receivables, inventory, and other noncash current assets are not expanding faster than sales. Scaling by sales ties the accrual leg to the revenue base that generates the margin, avoiding redundant industry normalization and reducing exposure to a pure asset-scaled accrual anomaly.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Gross Margin Inventory Overhang
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(NEG(invch), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Gross-margin improvement should reverse when it coincides with inventory cash absorption.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The signal focuses on margin expansion rather than the level of gross profitability, and isolates inventory buildup rather than repeating the earlier receivables-plus-inventory collection leg. Because invch is a cash-flow-statement impact, NEG(invch) identifies inventory accumulation; high scores therefore capture firms whose improving gross margins may reflect overproduction, cost capitalization, or demand weakness that has not yet hit earnings.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Pretax Profit Receivable Slippage
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, sale)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(NEG(recch), sale), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High pretax margins should underperform when they are paired with receivable buildup rather than customer cash collection.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This abandons the ambiguous tax-payable channel and instead tests whether reported pretax profitability is being converted into cash from customers. Since recch is negative when receivables rise, NEG(recch) captures collection slippage; the interaction targets profitable firms whose earnings may be pulled forward through accrual revenue recognition.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Depreciation Shortfall Profit
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(dpc, 1), at)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating profitability is less credible when depreciation and amortization charges are falling.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This replaces the cosmetic R&D add-back with a distinct long-term accrual mechanism: earnings can be inflated when depreciation expense is reduced through useful-life or residual-value assumptions. High scores identify firms with strong operating income alongside a depreciation shortfall, where profitability may be temporarily boosted by accounting estimates rather than durable cash economics.
